q: Who said, "Even a brick wants to be something"?
n: "Even a brick wants to be something" is a well-known line from Louis Kahn's lectures on materials. Source: Kahn, Louis Kahn: Essential Texts (ed. Twombly).

q: Who said, "Form and function are one"?
n: Frank Lloyd Wright said "Form and function are one," revising Sullivan's "form follows function." Source: Wright, An Autobiography; Frank Lloyd Wright Foundation.

q: The dictum "New situation requires a new architecture” belongs to.
n: The idea that a new situation requires a new architecture is attributed to Jean Nouvel, reflecting his context-specific approach. Source: Pritzker Architecture Prize, Jean Nouvel (2008) materials.

q: The dictum “Architecture is an expression of values” belongs to.
n: "Architecture is an expression of values" is a well-known Norman Foster statement. Source: Foster + Partners; Foster, interviews and lectures.

q: Who said, "God is in the details"?
n: "God is in the details" is commonly attributed to Mies van der Rohe. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Mies van der Rohe; New York Times obituary (1969).

q: Who said, "Less is more"?
n: "Less is more" is Mies van der Rohe's dictum. It sums up his minimalist approach of refined structure and open space without ornament. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Mies van der Rohe.

q: Who said, "To create, one must first question everything"?
n: "To create, one must first question everything" is attributed to Eileen Gray. Source: Eileen Gray biographies (Constant, Eileen Gray).

q: Who said, "Less is a bore"?
n: Robert Venturi answered Mies with "Less is a bore." Source: Venturi, Complexity and Contradiction in Architecture (1966).

q: Who wrote, "Form ever follows function"?
n: Louis Sullivan wrote "form ever follows function" in "The Tall Office Building Artistically Considered" (1896). Source: Sullivan (1896); Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: The dictum "Architecture seizes upon space, encompasses space and is space itself* belongs to.
n: The dictum "Architecture seizes upon space, encompasses space and is space itself" is attributed to Erich Mendelsohn. Source: Mendelsohn's writings and lectures (quoted in Zevi, Erich Mendelsohn).

q: Who said, "Form follows beauty"?
n: Oscar Niemeyer put beauty and free form first ("form follows beauty"). Source: Niemeyer, The Curves of Time.

q: Who said, "Lack of ornamentation is a sign of spiritual strength"?
n: Adolf Loos held that lack of ornament is a sign of spiritual strength. Source: Loos, Ornament and Crime (1908/1910).

q: Who described postmodern architecture as "double coding"?
n: Charles Jencks described postmodern architecture as "double coding," speaking to both experts and the public. Source: Jencks, The Language of Post-Modern Architecture (1977).

q: The dictum "Architects must have a razor-sharp sense of individuality” belongs to.
n: This dictum on the architect's sharp sense of individuality is attributed to Richard Neutra. Source: Neutra, Survival Through Design; Life and Shape.

q: Who warned that splitting life into separate problems splits the possibilities for good building art?
n: Alvar Aalto warned that splitting life into separate problems splits the possibilities for good building art. Source: Aalto, Sketches (ed. Schildt).

q: Who said design is not decorating functional forms but creating forms suited to the object and new technologies?
n: Peter Behrens held that design is creating forms suited to the object and new technologies, not decorating functional forms. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Peter Behrens; Buddensieg, Industriekultur.

q: Who said, "Philosophy is Morphosis"?
n: "Philosophy is Morphosis" is associated with Thom Mayne, founder of the firm Morphosis. Source: Morphosis Architects; Pritzker Prize (2005).

q: The dictum "A house is like a flower pot." belongs to.
n: The house-as-flower-pot analogy, a dwelling nurturing its occupants like soil, is attributed to Richard Neutra's biorealism. Source: Neutra, Survival Through Design (1954).

q: Who said, "A house is a machine for living in"?
n: Le Corbusier wrote "A house is a machine for living in." Source: Le Corbusier, Towards a New Architecture (1923).

q: Who said, "In all my works, light is an important controlling factor"?
n: Tadao Ando said light is an important controlling factor in all his works. Source: Ando, writings and Pritzker Prize (1995) materials.

q: Who is credited with "Simplicity is the ultimate sophistication"?
n: "Simplicity is the ultimate sophistication" is traditionally attributed to Leonardo da Vinci, though the attribution is uncertain. Source: Quote Investigator; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Who said, "Less is only more where more is no good"?
n: Frank Lloyd Wright said "Less is only more where more is no good." Source: Wright, writings (quoted in Pfeiffer, Frank Lloyd Wright).

q: The dictum "Function influence but does not dictate form’ belongs to.
n: "Function influences but does not dictate form" is attributed to Eero Saarinen. Source: Saarinen, Eero Saarinen on His Work (1962).

q: Who said, "Architecture is the reaching out for the truth"?
n: Louis Kahn said "Architecture is the reaching out for the truth." Source: Kahn, Louis Kahn: Essential Texts.

q: Who said, "Architecture is the art of how to waste space"?
n: Philip Johnson said "Architecture is the art of how to waste space." Source: Johnson, interviews (New York Times, 1964).

q: The dictum "Architecture is invention" was popularized by.
n: "Architecture is invention" is Oscar Niemeyer's dictum. Source: Niemeyer, The Curves of Time; Pritzker Prize (1988) materials.

q: Who said, "Architecture is the will of an epoch translated into space"?
n: Mies van der Rohe wrote "Architecture is the will of an epoch translated into space." Source: Mies van der Rohe, "Building Art and the Will of the Epoch" (1924).
